WoW: Forever

Feral — Cat Druid

Energy and combo points in Cat Form, on bleeds rather than big hits. From level 20 onward, one guide calls it "one of the fastest and most mobile specializations in the WoW Forever beta." Before 20 you are a bear.

WoW: Forever · Melee DPS · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Cat build has been tested. Bear and Cat share one talent tree and mostly one build; they have separate pages because the rotations, stat priorities and gear are completely different. No source has posted a level 30 build either — the cap only reached 30 on October 1 and none of the three has published one since — so the level 30 line below extends the published level 20 build using the full talent tree's point costs, not a build any guide has recommended. Blizzard's own caveat: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes."

What Cat is for

Damage out of stealth, at speed, and on bleeds that keep ticking while you reposition: Feral SwiftnessFeral SwiftnessTalentCastInstantIncreases your movement speed while in Cat Form by 30%, and increases your chance to Dodge by 4%. gives "a permanent 30% speed buff while in Cat Form" plus +4% dodge in all forms, and it now works indoors; you also have ProwlProwlLevel 20 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCooldown10 sec cooldownDurationUntil cancelledAllows the Druid to prowl around, but reduces your movement speed by 40%. Lasts until cancelled., shapeshifting breaks roots, and RipRipLevel 20 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCost30 ManaRangeMeleeDuration12 sec scales with attack power and runs 12 seconds off five combo points.

The published assessment, which measures solo kill speed — and it only applies from 20, when Cat Form arrives: one guide calls Feral "one of the fastest and most mobile specializations in the WoW Forever beta."

Cat Form now comes from a quest chain, not a trainer. "In WoW Forever, druids earn Cat Form with a quest chain at level 20. Your trainer sends you to Moonglade, the Great Cat Spirit asks for three relics hidden in the Stormrage Barrow Dens, and when you bring them back your trainer teaches you Cat Form, ProwlProwlLevel 20 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCooldown10 sec cooldownDurationUntil cancelledAllows the Druid to prowl around, but reduces your movement speed by 40%. Lasts until cancelled., ClawClawLevel 1 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCost25 ManaRangeMeleeClaw the enemy, causing 5 damage. and RipRipLevel 20 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCost30 ManaRangeMeleeDuration12 sec in one go." It is 2,885 experience in total, and the relics are party loot: "Five druids in a group loot the relic once instead of five times."

Stat priority

Agility first, then Strength, then Stamina.

The reason Agility leads is that "in cat form it is attack power, critical strike and armor at once."

The Forever-specific part reverses a Classic habit: your weapon's damage now counts in Cat Form. Cat Form's flat attack power was cut from 40 to 12 plus Agility, and abilities gained weapon-damage terms. Blizzard's own framing of the mechanism: auto-attack DPS in Cat Form now simply equals your weapon's DPS, at a fixed 1.0-second swing speed (2.5 seconds in Bear or Dire Bear Form), and weapon-damage abilities use the same numbers. The result: "the weapon here is chosen on its damage first, then on its stats." Published level-20 cat weapon picks are two-handers on both factions, held in both hands.

One source disputes the weapon-DPS priority outright. Three sources and the client data are against it, but the disagreement exists and no source publishes the actual conversion formula.

What Forever changed for Cat

  • The old FurorFurorTalentCastInstantGives you a 20% chance to gain 10 Rage when you shapeshift into Bear Form or Dire Bear Form. When you shift into Cat Form, you will regain 20% of the Energy you had when you were last in Cat Form, plus 2 Energy for each second you spent not in Bear Form, Cat Form, or Dire Bear Form, up to a maximum of 20 Energy. powershifting trick is dead, but Blizzard has deliberately reintroduced the gameplay in a different form — this is confirmed by Blizzard, not a player rumour. FurorFurorTalentCastInstantGives you a 20% chance to gain 10 Rage when you shapeshift into Bear Form or Dire Bear Form. When you shift into Cat Form, you will regain 20% of the Energy you had when you were last in Cat Form, plus 2 Energy for each second you spent not in Bear Form, Cat Form, or Dire Bear Form, up to a maximum of 20 Energy. was rewritten: instead of a flat 40 energy on entering Cat Form, five points let you regenerate Energy out of form "as if they were in Cat Form" — and Blizzard states the penalty in the same breath: "But if they go to Bear Form, all that Energy is lost, to prevent 'bear-weaving' gameplay." The numbers are client text, not published: the tooltip reads "regain 100% of the Energy you had when you were last in Cat Form, plus 10 Energy for each second you spent not in Bear Form, Cat Form, or Dire Bear Form, up to a maximum of 100" at 5/5, and "Leaving an empty bar and instantly re-entering supplies no flat refill." Blizzard then adds: "We realize this removed the 'power shifting' gameplay some players prize, so we have re-added that gameplay in a much more approachable way with the Shifting PowerShifting PowerTalentCastInstantCooldown16 sec cooldown talent in the Feral talent tree." That talent is live as of October 1 — see Shifting PowerShifting PowerTalentCastInstantCooldown16 sec cooldown above for its numbers.
  • Tiger's FuryTiger's FuryLevel 1 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantInstantly grants you Energy. was removed in the October 1 build — this is now live, not merely announced. Blizzard's class deep dive first flagged it under baseline shapeshifting changes: "Tiger's Fury: (Removed.) This has been replaced with a new Feral-specific talent called Shifting Power." The October 1 Development Notes confirm the ability itself is gone from the build — the datamined Tiger's FuryTiger's FuryLevel 1 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantInstantly grants you Energy. rework some guides still describe (no cost, 30-second cooldown, flat +15% physical damage) never shipped and will not appear; Shifting PowerShifting PowerTalentCastInstantCooldown16 sec cooldown (above) is what replaced it, live with full numbers the same day.
  • Bleeds carry the spec now, and ShredShredLevel 22 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCost60 ManaRangeMelee got stronger too. Blizzard: Shred’s "damage increased significantly to need less talent support to be effective" — no figures are published either way.
